reviews.text: The vet isn't a bad person, but he gets grumpy when you ask him questions. He doesn't perform unnecessary tests, but he also doesn't do necessary ones, and he doesn't even have the necessary testing equipment. It might be okay if you only want symptomatic treatment for elderly dogs or cats, but for younger pets, there's a very high chance of missing a serious illness, so I wouldn't recommend it. My cat went there for months, only to have a serious illness missed, and ended up needing surgery at another clinic. I deeply regret not giving up on this place sooner.

While it depends on the individual, I think treating your dog roughly is unacceptable.

I wouldn't entrust my dog ​​to them.

He seems kind at first glance, but lately he's given me the impression of being very scary. Even when he says the same things, his words and attitude are extremely cold and harsh. Maybe he was tired because it was nighttime... All I remember is that it pierced me hard when I was on the verge of tears. I couldn't feel grateful for it.

My Siberian cat had no appetite and lacked energy since morning, and was somewhat weak.
We suspected hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and had planned to take her to a specialist hospital soon, but because she became ill, we brought her to this hospital urgently.
The head veterinarian was off that day, so we were seen by a different doctor, who was very kind and examined her thoroughly. She received an IV drip as a temporary measure, and by evening she had finished all the Churu treats they gave her and was feeling much better.
Thank you very much. The resident cat was incredibly cute.

My cat usually becomes very unruly when I take her to the vet, but thanks to the very gentle and careful treatment I received at this hospital, she remained calm throughout the examination.

The head veterinarian is very kind and explains everything thoroughly and kindly!

Thank you so much.

I took my dog ​​to the vet to have his eyes checked.
As others have mentioned, it's a one-person operation, so the vet holds the dog really hard when administering eye drops...
My dog ​​had never been held that hard before, so I think it was just terrifying for him... and then they put in the eye drops.
I tried to help out by imitating what I'd seen, but the vet said, "Amateurs try to hold him there, but that just makes him move."

Until then, he was such a good dog that I could administer the eye drops myself, but since that day, he won't let me anymore...
He's completely traumatized...💧

They've been running the hospital for many years, so they probably have the knowledge, but I think it must be quite difficult to handle animals without an assistant.
The teacher and his wife are nice people. They are involved in cat rescue activities.

I wouldn't even give it one star.
I had a very unpleasant experience with how they handled my ill-tempered cat.
It's true that drawing blood from an agitated cat is difficult. I felt sorry for putting my cat through that situation, but the enraged vet hurled unpleasant words at me.
Isn't it wrong to speak to a worried owner based solely on emotion? My trust in the vet completely vanished.
I had read other people's reviews about their cats before and thought something like that might happen, but now I understand completely.
My cat is a precious member of my family, so I want to be able to say that I'm glad I chose this hospital, knowing that I had a good experience with this vet in the end, no matter what happens.
I had been going there for a while, but I took this opportunity to go to another hospital, and they treated my cat with genuine care, so I switched hospitals.

My dog ​​is a regular patient here. You can really tell the doctor loves animals. He's always cheerful and gives accurate diagnoses, so I highly recommend him. I hope to continue using his services in the future.

I wouldn't even give it one star.

When I left my two cats (from my parents' house) with them, they both came back bleeding. When I called to inquire about the situation, they didn't even apologize until I specifically asked for it.

This was my first time using this hospital's pet hotel.

They said a check-up was necessary before leaving them, so I took them in. When I returned from the check-up, one of my cats was bleeding from the base of its claw.

I think it was probably because the cat struggled a bit when being put in the carrier, and the hospital staff forced it shut, pinching the claw. However, since it was the cat's fault and I thought it might have been a fluke, I didn't contact them at the time.

I was a little worried, but I thought they were professionals and it would be alright, so I left them there on a different day.

I was able to pick them up earlier than the scheduled date, so I contacted them to ask if I could change the date and time. They said it was fine, so my sister went to pick them up.

When we arrived at the hospital, the doctor was bleeding from his hand and showed us the wound. He seemed very angry and, in a very firm tone, told us we couldn't take care of the cats and banned us from the hospital.

My sister is not yet an adult, so she was intimidated by his demeanor and couldn't ask for more details.

When we got home, both cats were bleeding from their hands, and they were limping and bleeding when they walked, indicating the injuries were quite severe. My mother and I called the hospital to ask for an explanation, and despite the late hour, the head doctor answered.

However, the doctor only talked about his own injuries and how things would have been much worse if another staff member had been involved, and offered no apology.

Only when I apologized to the doctor for our cats injuring him and said, "Shouldn't you apologize first, Doctor?" did he finally say, "I'm sorry."

It seems that the clinic was already operating with only one staff member when we changed the date and time, and I apologize for the inconvenience caused. However, when we left our cat at another hospital, it didn't act up at all and came back without any problems, and this is the first time something like this has happened.

The cat that bit the doctor is usually timid and doesn't have the courage to threaten, so I think it must have been treated very coldly.

They explained the circumstances, and I looked into it afterward, and I think it's not uncommon for cats to act up.

I understand that it can be a serious matter if an animal bites, and I am deeply sorry that the doctor was injured.

However, I didn't sense any sense of regret in their apology for injuring a family member.

Honestly, I don't think the director is fit to be responsible for a life.

Many of the people who have posted positive reviews seem to have dogs, so perhaps they are better at treating dogs, but I would not recommend entrusting your cat to them.

I was told I'm banned from their clinic, but I will never ask them again.
